.rail: * A count of what the model labelled, not of what it got right — there is no ground truth on a patient scan. Positions with no tooth material at all are named below, and an absent third molar is an ordinary dentition rather than a miss.
li 3 tooth/teeth outside the plausible volume range: 18 (126 mm3), 26 (218 mm3), 28 (149 mm3)
li canal has 5 significant component(s); expected 2 (one per side)
li 2 contralateral pair(s) differ by more than 30% in volume, worst 12/22 at 59%
li Scan was stored LPS; reoriented to RPI for inference and mapped back for the download.
* Facts about the image, not findings about the segmentation. A structure cut by the edge of the field of view is the wrong size because the scan stops, and that is not an error to correct.
li 699,511 predicted voxel(s) were discarded outside the padded box around the dentition — the model labels cranial structures this product does not claim

* ToothFairy3F_041 comes from the ToothFairy3 research dataset and carries an expert annotation; it was held out of training, so this model has never seen it. That is what makes a measurement possible here and impossible on an upload — the Findings panel above is what is left when there is nothing to measure against. One case, and the easiest kind: read it as a demonstration that the numbers are real, not as what your own scan would score.
* This is not a patient scan.
* Lower right lateral incisor (42) 0.80 · Upper right second premolar (15) 0.80 · Lower right second molar (47) 0.80

* The drawn wall sits up to 0.46 mm inside the true wall at the 95th percentile (worst single point 2.96 mm). This is the direction that costs clearance: a plan drawn on this outline believes it has that much more bone than it has.
* 94% of the annotated canal covered · 0.41 mm inward

* The drawn wall sits up to 0.47 mm inside the true wall at the 95th percentile (worst single point 3.14 mm). This is the direction that costs clearance: a plan drawn on this outline believes it has that much more bone than it has.

* The drawn wall sits up to 0.22 mm inside the true wall at the 95th percentile (worst single point 1.50 mm). This is the direction that costs clearance: a plan drawn on this outline believes it has that much more bone than it has.

* The drawn wall sits up to 0.39 mm inside the true wall at the 95th percentile (worst single point 1.46 mm). This is the direction that costs clearance: a plan drawn on this outline believes it has that much more bone than it has.

* Strict protocol: a structure absent from both the annotation and the prediction is excluded rather than scored 1.0. Dice is unforgiving of small objects — a canal one voxel wide loses a third of its score to a one-voxel wall shift — so read the millimetre figures for those, not the ratio. Computed in the 45-structure space shown here; these are not challenge leaderboard numbers.
h3 How accurate is the model?
h4 The structures an implant plan depends on
* Inward error is the direction that costs clearance: the drawn wall sitting the true one. The p95 is what the implant verdicts deduct; the worst single point is quoted and never subtracted.
h4 What this does not claim
* The exact model output, on the grid you uploaded. Use this for anything measured.
* The upload was not DICOM, so there was no series to reference. Import BOTH the CT folder and RS.dcm — the structure set alone will not load.
* Every measurement on this page, plus timings and VRAM.
* Per-structure STL: hover a structure above and click ⤓ (41 meshes, smoothed and decimated).
